svg.text: K5b PEELING, CORING, STONING — three generic mechanisms
No single-purpose peelers: a spit on the roll axis, the press with a perforated plate, and a rough pot on P0.
spit 120–150 rpm, blade 3–6 N, shoe 1 / 3 / 5 mm
press-peel 0.3–3 kN on the 4.5 mm plate
knurled pot 250 rpm, stops at < 5 % skin
The fork on the roll axis spins the potato; the handler draws it pole to pole
past the sprung Y-blade on the peeler post. Peel falls into the tray.
Y-blade on a flexure, depth shoe
handler draws Y, pole to pole
B Press-peel: skin and stone stay, flesh passes
Banana and avocado are pressed whole on the 4.5 mm plate: banana bread
and guacamole; the skin and stone stay on the plate and go with it to waste.
Potatoes tumble on a rough floor liner at 250 rpm under a water spray;
the scraper on the crosshead is the deflector. Camera stops at < 5 % skin.
Coring: plunged by the press foot
A pepper stands stalk-up in a nest on the anvil; the Ø 42 plug corer with
a cone is pushed down by the foot, then ejected against a fixed pin.

g.text: 1/3 Three generic mechanisms cover the peeling list; corers are plunged by the same press
2/3 A: spit and post peels pole to pole · B: press pushes flesh through the plate, skin stays · C: P0 tumbles potatoes on a rough floor
3/3 Coring: the plug comes out in the corer and is pushed off against the fixed pin at the rinse seat
